+\paragraph{What is new.}
+The question is global support selection, rather than the local law within
+one face. Herv\'e and Ledoux~\cite{herveledoux2013} give quantitative density
+local limits for finite-state Markov additive processes, while occupation
+large deviations describe exponential costs~\cite{dv1975,gnw2024,bgl2024,landim2023}.
+Here the exit cost must be compared with a different lattice dimension on
+each support. We control maxima across all admissible faces, approximate
+the lattice law by killed-chain densities, and compute the constants that
+resolve first-order ties. The complete graph gives an explicit instance
+where the exponential costs alone leave every size tied.
+
+\paragraph{Scope.}
+The local estimates are uniform on compact subsets of irreducible faces
+with positive start mass. They do not extend uniformly to the boundary.
+The first-order support rule allows reducible faces, but we do not give a
+general sharp expansion for them. We locate pairwise crossings under the
+stated hypotheses, without proving uniqueness for arbitrary chains.
+
+Theorem~\ref{thm:hull} reads the first-order winners from the convex hull
+of $(\lambda_F,|F|-1)$, and Section~\ref{sec:worked} gives a four-state cycle
+example. A small-set mode trades the cost of leaving against the number of
+count vectors sharing its mass. As $\tau$ increases the winning size can
+only grow. The exact three-state example in Figure~\ref{fig:simplex} shows
+this competition at finite $N$.
